concerns.concern: The Raman symmetry argument uses a scattering geometry with Y and Z in the bc plane but not along the crystal axes. In that geometry Ag and Bg modes are not separated, and twin domains mix the channels further, so counting 31 modes in yy against 24 allowed Ag modes is invalid.
concerns.quote: are in the (bc) plane but not aligned with a particular axis

concerns.concern: The new Raman lines below the density-wave transition could come from zone folding or amplitudon/phason modes of an incommensurate modulation that keeps the 2/m point group. Claiming point-group lowering and a 'third structural phase' (Pc/P21) is therefore not justified, especially since XRD sees no satellites or lattice distortion.
concerns.quote: Based on this we propose a third structural phase

concerns.concern: Excluding the Bmab intermediate phase relies on β deviations near the onset that are well below 0.1°. The authors themselves call that level close to experimental accuracy, and twinning may cause systematic errors in it. A better fit with B21/a, which has more parameters, is expected anyway, so a significance test or Bmab-violating reflections are needed.
concerns.quote: is much better as shown in Table S4 in the SI [39]

concerns.concern: The total mode count of 51 exceeds the 48 allowed modes by only 3. Modes leaking into both channels, combination features or electronic features could account for that margin. Table I also wrongly includes the three acoustic modes in the Pc/P21 counts.
concerns.quote: Since we measure a total of 51 phonon modes at low temperature

concerns.concern: The DFT result depends on starting structure and force tolerance, and the total energy is converged only to 1 mHa, likely far more than the phase energy differences. Smearing, spin polarization and k-mesh convergence are unspecified. Calling the result 'unequivocal' is too strong without constrained-symmetry enthalpy comparisons.
concerns.quote: Within this cell the total energy was found converged within 1 mHa

concerns.concern: The ±0.04 GPa agreement of DFT critical pressures comes from extrapolating three-point fits with assumed exponents on a ~1 GPa grid. Secondary order parameters must vanish together in any case, so a narrow Bmab window could go undetected.
concerns.quote: the three order parameters all nullify at the same critical pressure

concerns.concern: The paper calls the transition both weakly first-order, because of the observed jump in β, and continuous. This matters because in a first-order scenario an intermediate phase or coexistence cannot be excluded by extrapolation. The review also asks whether hysteresis or coexistence was checked.
concerns.quote: as the transition from 4/mmm to 2/m is continuous

concerns.concern: Mixed-order (q1±q2) superlattice reflections sit at positions forbidden in every B21/a twin domain, so twinning cannot produce them. If they are real, they contradict the 2-fold B-centred model. If they are multiple-diffraction or λ/2 artefacts, that needs to be shown.
concerns.quote: along with mixed-order satellite reflections corresponding to linear combinations

concerns.concern: The estimate that 3 GPa shrinks b by 1% appears inconsistent with the measured bulk moduli and in-plane compressibility, which imply roughly 5–10 GPa. The PBE-induced error on the DFT Pc may therefore be several GPa, and the estimate is not the 'most pessimistic' one.

No resistivity, magnetization or heat-capacity data confirm the density-wave transition in these flux-grown crystals, and the oxygen stoichiometry is not reported. Sample differences could therefore explain the absence of XRD satellites, and the link between the Raman changes and the DW remains inferential.
concerns.quote: Both techniques confirm the La:Ni 4:3 atomic ratio.

concerns.concern: The claim that superconductivity emerges only in the tetragonal phase is not tested here, since no transport or magnetic data under pressure are reported. Reported superconducting onset pressures span 5–40 GPa, some below the measured low-T boundary.
concerns.quote: This affirms that superconductivity emerges only once the system is restored to the tetragonal phase under pressure.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature critical pressure found here (10.5–11.3 GPa) differs by about 4 GPa from the ~15 GPa in the cited literature. Possible causes such as pressure medium, hydrostaticity or stoichiometry are not discussed.
concerns.quote: The lattice is F4/mmm at 11.3 GPa

concerns.concern: The phase boundary between ambient pressure and ~10 GPa has no data, so the 'linear suppression' from 1030 K to 20 K is an assumed interpolation. The low-T points also show flattening.
concerns.quote: Dashed line serving as a visual guide to indicate the linear suppression

concerns.concern: The bulk modulus rises unusually strongly from 300 K to 80 K. The EOS fits span the phase boundary, and the EOS order and K′ are not stated, so the K0(T) trend may be a fitting artefact.
Calling the octahedra 'perfect' at 15 GPa is misleading. Only the tilt vanishes; the octahedra remain axially distorted, as the paper itself describes.
concerns.quote: At 15 GPa, the octahedra is perfect.

concerns.concern: Different values (135 K, 130 K, 120–150 K, ~120 K) are quoted for the density-wave or symmetry-lowering temperature without a stated criterion or comparison to the literature.
